deep_analysis:
Portfolio is flat (0 open trades) — and in this regime that is the correct position, not a problem to fix. BTC is at EMA300 with LEAN_BEAR linreg and STRONG_DOWN trend quality on the 4h, while the 15m shows a SHORT-BIAS-vs-LONG-BIAS conflict (15m LONG_BIAS bounce inside a 4h SHORT_BIAS macro). Volatility is LOW. This is chop, and chop is where our hard_max_loss trades die.

The 48h data is unambiguous on direction: 38 LONGs lost -1.93 USDT at 36.8% WR while 15 SHORTs gained +0.10 at 40% WR. We are structurally long-heavy because pump-chain+, bb-bounce-v2-long+, and doji-bottom-long generate LONGs far more often than their SHORT counterparts. Every LONG RSI band lost money. The winning side was SHORTs at RSI 30-40 (100% WR, n=2) and 60-70 (67% WR, n=3). We were not on that side because signal generation defaults to LONG.

The exit-reason breakdown confirms the philosophy: atr_sl_hit (n=14, -1.27) plus hard_max_loss (n=8, -0.96) = 22 trades that died at SL before the trail could arm. These are chop entries, not bad stop management. The trail family (profit-monster-trail: 10/11 wins, +0.43; atr_trail_hit: 2/3, +0.07) wins because it enters in trends with room to run. The lever is trending-vs-ranging discrimination at entry, not wider stops.

The pending signal queue has self-corrected: 15 SHORTs vs 1 LONG pending right now (pump-chain-, ichimoku-, r2-trend-short). That alignment with the 4h SHORT_BIAS is healthy. The structural gap is that pump-chain+ and doji-bottom-long still fire LONGs into this regime — doji-bottom-long specifically interprets oversold as a buy signal in a market where oversold means still going lower (7d: n=16, 31% WR, -0.97).

AI trader: last pick (SAND LONG, rejected at 05:34) is stale. This hour I picked GRASS SHORT (precheck PASS, R:R 1.50, fading -2.5% over 3h, RSI 39.2 in the winning 30-40 SHORT band). GOAT and GMX SHORT also passed precheck but GOAT is in a local LONG_BIAS regime and GMX was rising +1.16% over 3h — both would have been wrong-side entries.

pattern_alerts:
PATTERN 1 — WRONG-SIDE DIRECTION (verified, 48h, PostgreSQL):
n=53 trades. LONG: n=38, pnl=-1.93, WR=36.8%. SHORT: n=15, pnl=+0.10, WR=40.0%. 71% of trades were LONG against a SHORT_BIAS macro. Every LONG RSI band (using meta_rsi, not entry_rsi_14) lost money: <30: 0% WR, 30-40: 0% WR, 40-50: 44% WR, 50-60: 43% WR, 60-70: 33% WR. WINNING SIDE: SHORTs at meta_rsi 30-40 (100% WR, +0.04) and 60-70 (67% WR, +0.40). WHY WE WEREN'T ON IT: pump-chain+, bb-bounce-v2-long+, and doji-bottom-long dominate signal generation and all emit LONGs. The SHORT signals (pump-chain-, volume-buildup-) exist but fire less often. Structural long-bias in a SHORT_BIAS market.

PATTERN 2 — CHOP ENTRIES DIE BEFORE TRAIL ARMS (verified, 48h, PostgreSQL):
atr_sl_hit n=14 WR=7.1% pnl=-1.27 plus hard_max_loss n=8 WR=0% pnl=-0.96 = 22 trades, -2.23 USDT total. 52/56 hard_max_loss trades historically never reached +0.40% for trail to arm. These are entries into ranging coins where price hits SL before any trend materializes. WINNING SIDE: the trail family — profit-monster-trail 10/11 wins (+0.43), atr_trail_hit 2/3 (+0.07), UNIVERSAL_MAX_HOLD 2/2 (+0.14) — enters in trends with room to run. WHY WE WEREN'T ON IT: the signal quality gate does not distinguish trending from ranging. LOW volatility + SLOW velocity right now makes this worse.

PATTERN 3 — doji-bottom-long IS A REGIME-BLIND FALLING KNIFE (verified, 7d):
n=16, WR=31%, pnl=-0.97. Recent losers: ZEN -0.11 (meta_rsi 29.5), CRV -0.10 (meta_rsi 39.8). This signal interprets oversold RSI as a buy. In a SHORT_BIAS regime, oversold = still going lower. WINNING SIDE: SHORT the same coins during the dump. WHY WE WEREN'T ON IT: the signal has no regime gate — it fires on doji bottoms regardless of whether the 4h trend is down. Brain auditor item: add a BTC 4h SHORT_BIAS regime filter to doji-bottom-long.

PATTERN 4 — SHORT BANDS THAT WIN (verified, 48h meta_rsi, n=15 SHORTs):
RSI 30-40: n=2, 100% WR, +0.04. RSI 60-70: n=3, 67% WR, +0.40. RSI 40-50: n=5, 0% WR, -0.27. RSI 50-60: n=1, 0% WR, -0.08. The winning SHORT entry is either deeply oversold (30-40) or overextended (60-70) — the middle band (40-50) loses. Note: the SHORT_RSI_HARD_FLOOR=45 gate blocks the 30-40 band that has 100% WR. This is a tension the brain auditor should examine: the safety gate may be blocking our best SHORT entries. Sample sizes are small (n=2-5) so this is directional, not conclusive.
